title: Exchange Rate Systems
welcome_lead: Floating, fixed and managed - three ways to handle the currency.
meta_desc: A-Level Exchange Rates: floating vs fixed systems.
final_note: Each regime trades flexibility against credibility differently.

concepts.def: Determined by market supply and demand for currency; UK has floated since 1992 Black Wednesday ERM exit.
Government pegs rate via reserves and rates; Hong Kong dollar pegged to USD since 1983.
Central bank intervenes occasionally without explicit target; describes most major currencies in practice.
Purchasing power parity: exchange rates should equalise price levels; The Economist's Big Mac Index estimates PPP.
Depreciation improves trade balance only if sum of import and export PEDs exceeds 1.
Trade balance worsens before improving after depreciation as quantities adjust slower than prices.

walkthroughs.body_html: Most large economies float. Markets set the rate; the central bank uses interest rates for monetary policy and lets the currency move where it likes.
Fixed systems require the central bank to hold reserves and intervene to defend the peg. The Chinese yuan and Hong Kong dollar use variants of fixed regimes.
The Mundell trilemma: a country can have any two of free capital flow, fixed rate, and independent monetary policy - not all three at once.
